chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:

Abu Zarr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'May Allah condemn the world on my behalf. [I was content] after two loaves of barley, with which I would have lunch with one and dinner with the other, and after two woolen garments, with which I would wear one as a lower garment and the other as an upper garment.'

key_terms.أَتَرَدَّى: I wear as an upper garment
key_terms.أَتَّزِرُ: I wear as a lower garment

ai.seo_question: What did Abu Zarr say about his simple lifestyle and contentment with the world?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Abu Zarr al-Ghifari’s embodiment of zuhd (asceticism) through his minimal material needs, specifically two barley loaves and two woolen garments, serving as a practical model for spiritual detachment. In Shia tradition, this exemplifies the virtue of kifayah (sufficiency), where the soul is freed from worldly attachment to focus on divine remembrance, a theme central to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings on modest living.
